note.question: How does endogenous trust scores instead of monetary transfers contribute to repeated project-funding mechanism?
note.overview: Privately informed managers repeatedly compete for internal project funding from a principal. The trust-and-evaluate allocation rule is a dynamic nonmonetary mechanism under which truthful reporting is proved to be an epsilon-Bayesian Nash equilibrium while principal value approaches the first best.

source.section: Trust-and-Evaluate: A Dynamic Nonmonetary Mechanism for Internal Capital Allocation
source.quote: Our setting consists of a principal and multiple agents.
In other words, the first-best setting is a centralized setting in which there is only one decision-maker, that is, the principal.

Budget-Feasible Mechanisms The literature on “budget-feasible” mechanisms ana­ lyzes variants of the following basic problem: A buyer has a fixed budget for purchasing a set of items from agents who privately know the costs of the items.

components.explanation: The horizon is infinite and partitioned into phases of L periods. At the start of a phase every agent receives a trust endowment. In each period, active agents privately observe project estimates and report them. The principal applies the first-best project-selection rule to the reports of active agents.

components.label: Truthful epsilon-Bayesian Nash equilibrium under the trust-and-evaluate mechanism
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Truthful epsilon-Bayesian Nash equilibrium under the trust-and-evaluate mechanism. Theorem 1 states that for every epsilon greater than zero, sufficiently long phases and a suitable tolerance level make truthful reporting an epsilon-Bayesian Nash equilibrium and place principal utility within epsilon of first best. Proposition 1 bounds any unilateral deviation, Lemma 2 shows truthful agents stay active with high probability, and Proposition 2 lower-bounds truthful funding utility. Theorem 2 generalizes the result and Proposition 3 gives explicit convergence rates.

components.label: Solution or estimation method
components.explanation: The authors construct a phase-based allocation mechanism, normalize trust updates by first-best allocation probabilities and value, and combine stochastic ordering, order statistics, tail bounds, and limiting arguments to prove incentive and performance guarantees. A data-informed dynamic-programming study evaluates practical phase lengths, and a general theorem extends the mechanism to multidimensional types and partial allocations.
